QF.id: VII Introduction to Securities Broking Operations_16

question.text: An Immediate or Cancel (IOC) order is best described as:

answer.text: An order that must be executed immediately; any unmatched portion is cancelled instantly
An order that remains in the system until cancelled by the trader
An order that is valid for the entire trading day
An order that gets activated only when a trigger price is reached

explanation.text: The Logic: An IOC order is released into the market immediately, and the unmatched portion is cancelled immediately. Partial matching is possible: any part that finds a counter trades, and the remainder is cancelled instantly. The Trap: A Day order stays in the system until end of day, and GTC/GTD orders persist across days. Confusing these time-condition order types with IOC misses the immediate-execute-or-cancel nature of IOC. Note: The Series VII workbook (pp.94-95) is the controlling source for the IOC definition and for the contrasts with Day and GTC/GTD orders.
